To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Antibiotics can be used as growth promoters in food-producing animals.
the use of antibiotic drugs in the treatment of bacterial diseases has led to the development of antibiotic resistance.

1) the use of antibiotics in animal production is a major driver of resistance; 2) the use of antimicrobial drugs is associated with an increased risk of AMR in humans; and 3) the use of veterinary antimicrobial drugs is a major driver for the emergence of AMR in food animals, and this AMR is a threat to human health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of problems, which we call the "antibiotics resistance problem".
the development of a novel class of antibiotics that target the bacterial cell wall and are active against a wide range of Gram-positive pathogens, including MRSA.
the study of the effects of the antibiotic resistance genes (ARG) on the microbial ecology and the fate of ARG in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

antibiotics are an essential part of the management of many diseases, but their overuse, especially in the developing world, is leading to the emergence of resistant strains, and that the prudent and rational use of these agents is of utmost importance.

there are no antibiotics that have been proven to be effective in the treatment of mastitis in cows, and the only antibiotic that has been shown to be effective in mastitis treatment in goats, is the antibiotic penicillin.
the antibiotic resistance in bacteria is caused by the overuse of antibiotics, the misuse of antibiotics, and the lack of hygiene in hospitals and clinics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the combination of a high level of antibiotics in the environment, together with the high level of antibiotic resistance, can have a significant impact on the ecosystem.
we have demonstrated that the use of antibiotics in the dairy cattle industry is a major factor contributing to antibiotic resistance in humans.

we have demonstrated that a combination of a small amount of antibiotics and a large amount of probiotics can be effective in treating mastitis, and that the probiotic bacteria can survive and colonize in the udder and in the milk of cows with mastitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of antibiotics in animal feed is a major driver for the evolution of antibiotic resistance in bacteria.

antibiotic resistance is a global problem and that it is important for us all to be aware that the misuse and overuse of antibiotics can lead to the evolution of resistant bacteria, which are more difficult and expensive to treat.
the use of antibiotics is a double edged sword and it is not possible to completely eliminate the use of these drugs.
